guide:
## Overview

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a hybrid Mamba-MoE vision-language model with image and
video input. The profiles below follow the NVIDIA cookbook's configurations on
`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0`. The page opens on the one-H200 NVFP4 configuration.
Every generated command uses the full Hugging Face model ID as its served name.

## Prerequisites

- Pull the pinned vLLM image and make the selected checkpoint available from
  Hugging Face. LiLiCorr on DGX Spark also needs its separate draft checkpoint.
- The NVFP4 checkpoint's safetensors index reports 75.01 GB; the recipe's 91 GB
  minimum includes the schema's 20% allowance. The BF16 index reports 248.91 GB,
  giving a 299 GB minimum by the same method.
- These are weight allowances, not a guarantee that every context and batch
  setting fits. Use the cookbook's per-hardware memory settings.

## Hardware configurations

| Hardware | Variant | TP | Context | Cookbook workload |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1x H200 | NVFP4 | 1 | 114,688 | Multimodal, MTP 3 |
| 2x H100 | NVFP4 | 2 | 114,688 | Multimodal, MTP 3 |
| 4x H100 | BF16 | 4 | 114,688 | Multimodal, MTP 3 |
| 1x GB200 | NVFP4 | 1 | 114,688 | Text only, MTP 5 |
| 2x GB200 | BF16 | 2 | 114,688 | Multimodal, MTP 5 |
| 4x GB200 | NVFP4 or BF16 4x | 4 | 28,672 | Text only, MTP 5 |
| 1x DGX Spark | NVFP4 | 1 | 114,688 | Text-only MTP 5 or LiLiCorr 7 |
| 1x RTX Pro 6000 | NVFP4 | 1 | 16,384 | MTP 5 |

Select the matching Hardware and Variant pills to generate these commands.
On GB200, choose BF16 with TP 2 for image or video input: the 1x NVFP4 and
4x variants use `--chat-template-content-format string` for text workloads.
DGX Spark defaults to its text-only MTP command; the LiLiCorr mode uses the
separate DFlash draft checkpoint and changes its concurrency and memory budget.
The BF16 notebook examples allow local media paths under `/`; turn on the
optional Local Media feature only when serving trusted clients that need it.

The cookbook also validates NVFP4 on 2x A100 with an 8,192-token allocation.
A100 is not in the site's hardware taxonomy, so use its command directly:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name nemotron-3.5-super \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --speculative_config.method mtp \
  --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens 5 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3
```

Use `nemotron-3.5-super` as the client model name for this A100 command.

The cookbook also provides 1M-token text-only commands. They use
`--language-model-only` and `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1`; apply those
complete commands from the notebook when the full window is needed. The
selectable configurations here retain shorter hardware-specific allocations.

## Client usage

Send requests to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1` with model
`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4` or the BF16 model ID,
depending on the selected variant. The cookbook includes image and video
requests, tool calls, and reasoning output examples.

## References

- [NVIDIA vLLM cookbook](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Nemotron/blob/main/usage-cookbook/Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL/vllm_cookbook.ipynb)
- [NVFP4 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4)
- [BF16 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16)
- [LiLiCorr draft checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr)
- [RedHatAI FP8 model card](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-FP8)
- [RedHatAI DSpark model card](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B.dspark)
